newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Astra posts 10 pct rise in profits.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Astra posts 10 pct rise in profits.

text.p: Swedish pharmaceutical heavyweight Astra AB Wednesday chalked up a 10 percent increase in 1996 profits, in line with analyst's expectations.

Astra reported a rise in pretax profit to 13.2 billion crowns ($1.77 billion), or 15.33 crowns a share ($2.05), compared with pre-tax profits of 12.06 billion crowns ($1.62 billion), or 14.22 crowns a share ($1.90), in 1995.

Sales rose 9 percent to 38.99 billion crowns ($5.37 billion) from 35.8 billion crowns ($4.8 billion) in the previous year. In a Reuters poll, analysts expected a profit of 13.17 billion crowns ($1.77 billion).
Analysts said Astra should keep growing, pointing to several new drugs and dismissing concerns about expiring patents on Astra's blockbuster anti-ulcer drug Losec.

Worlwide sales and licensing revenues from Losec accounted for about two-thirds of Astra'a sales in 1996. Losec patents expire in 2001 in the United States, in Britain in 2002, Germany and Sweden in 2003, and France, Japan and Spain in 2004.

Analysts said that while Losec sales will likely fall once those patents expire, the company has a strong portfolio of other drugs and may have new products developed by the time the patents begin to expire.
The company's other products include treatments for asthma, high blood pressure, impotence and osteoporosis.
Astra stock closed 1.5 crown (20 cents) lower at 385.5 crowns ($51.76).
